stories.headline: Coalition instability deepens as Nausėda and LSDP clash over Dawn of Nemunas deadline
stories.summary: President Nausėda issued a public ultimatum warning that if the Social Democrats fail to make a decision on ejecting Dawn of Nemunas from the coalition by end of May, the moment will pass. New LSDP chairman Sinkevičius, elected on May 1, said he needs up to a month to decide, while a party-commissioned poll showed voters split on whether to continue the coalition. President Nausėda also voiced doubts about governance in ministries under Dawn of Nemunas, and PM Ruginienė downplayed the coalition question as not the most important political issue.

stories.headline: Latvia drone incursion from Russia triggers Baltic NATO air-defense alarm, Lithuania scrambles jets
stories.summary: On May 7, multiple drones crossed into Latvian airspace from Russia, with two crashing — one near an oil storage facility in Rēzekne causing a brief fire. Latvia scrambled jets and summoned Russia's ambassador; Lithuania's jets flew from Šiauliai to patrol Latvian airspace. Lithuania and Latvia jointly called on NATO to boost regional air defenses. Latvia's defense minister offered to resign after detection technology failed. A second drone remained missing as of May 9.

stories.headline: Seimas strips ex-PM Paluckas of parliamentary immunity amid corruption investigation
stories.summary: The Seimas voted to lift former Prime Minister Gintauto Paluckas's legal immunity, enabling prosecutors to pursue criminal charges related to alleged conflicts of interest in his family's business dealings. Paluckas said he intends to remain in the Seimas; PM Ruginienė said the decision is his alone; President Nausėda urged him to act more principally; LSDP chairman Sinkevičius said the party would not pressure him to leave the faction.

stories.headline: Lithuania's first HIMARS rocket artillery systems unveiled at Lockheed Martin factory in Arkansas
stories.summary: Lithuania and Lockheed Martin jointly unveiled Lithuania's first M142 HIMARS multiple launch rocket systems at a ceremony in Camden, Arkansas. The systems were formally handed over to the Lithuanian Armed Forces, marking a significant boost in precision long-range strike capability. Lockheed Martin also established a legal entity in Lithuania, signaling deeper industrial cooperation.

stories.headline: Ruginienė approval falls sharply as 74% disapprove and Blinkevičiūtė rated more suitable as PM
stories.summary: New polling data showed PM Ruginienė's cabinet disapproval at 74% in April, her personal rating falling to fifth place among potential prime ministerial candidates, behind MEP Vilija Blinkevičiūtė who declined the post last year. Commentary compared Ruginienė's trajectory to the troubled tenure of former Seimas Speaker Graužinienė.

stories.headline: Lithuania signs €6.4 billion EU SAFE defense loan for military modernization
stories.summary: Lithuania signed the European Security Action via Enablement (SAFE) loan agreement on May 9 in Vilnius, securing nearly €6.375 billion in long-term EU loans for defense. The funds will support full equipment of a new land forces division, heavy armored vehicles, and Baltic Defense Line fortifications. PM Ruginienė noted the largest share will go to air defense; the deal was signed by the Finance and Defense ministers alongside EU Commissioners Kubilius and Serafin.

stories.headline: Two railway derailments ruled technical failures; government orders critical infrastructure protection plan within two weeks
stories.summary: After two train derailments on the same weekend, PM Ruginienė convened the National Security Commission and announced that investigations found no evidence of sabotage — causes were technical and human error. She ordered Lithuanian Railways (LTG) and the Transport Ministry to submit a detailed critical infrastructure protection plan within two weeks.

stories.headline: Nausėda and Ruginienė signal Lithuania ready to join Strait of Hormuz coalition
stories.summary: Following a US invitation to join a coalition ensuring safe navigation in the Strait of Hormuz, President Nausėda said Lithuania's plans to contribute are unchanged regardless of shifting US actions in the region, and that the State Defense Council will meet shortly. PM Ruginienė described reopening the strait as a major European interest. Latvia also confirmed receiving the US invitation.

stories.headline: Nausėda signals Lithuania ready to host additional US troops as Poland-Lithuania conduct joint exercises
stories.summary: During joint military exercises on the Lithuanian-Polish border attended by both presidents, Nausėda said Lithuania is prepared to host additional US forces currently stationed in Germany. He emphasized the strategic importance of the US military presence in Europe. Media noted the backdrop of Trump's announcement of withdrawing 5,000 troops from Germany, prompting Poland and Lithuania to compete to host them.

stories.headline: Nausėda urges Lithuania to leverage EU Council Presidency for greater influence; Europe Day marked
stories.summary: President Nausėda met with teams preparing for Lithuania's EU Council Presidency (commencing January 2026 second half) and called on them to use the chairmanship to raise Lithuania's international profile, involving municipalities, cultural institutions, and communities. The week also saw Lithuania mark the 22nd anniversary of EU accession with a ceremony in Vilnius where PM Ruginienė and EU Commissioner Micallef raised the EU flag.

stories.summary: PM Ruginienė traveled to Yerevan to participate in the 8th European Political Community Summit, engaging in panel discussions with European leaders on security, Russia's war in Ukraine, and the ECAD anti-narcotics coalition.

stories.headline: Bank of Lithuania proposes anti-fraud package requiring banks to compensate scam victims
stories.summary: The Bank of Lithuania submitted over 20 proposed legislative amendments to the Finance Ministry to strengthen anti-fraud measures, including giving banks the authority to freeze suspicious payments, mandating inter-bank information sharing on fraud, and requiring banks to compensate customers who lose money to financial fraud.

stories.headline: Banks revise down Lithuania 2026 GDP forecasts amid inflation and global uncertainty
stories.summary: SEB Bank forecast 3.2% GDP growth and 5.7% inflation for Lithuania in 2026, while Swedbank trimmed its GDP forecast to 3.0% from 3.5% (still fastest in the Baltics). The Bank of Lithuania issued a wide minimum wage forecast range of 6–12% for next adjustment. An Estonian economist sparked debate by arguing Lithuania has not clearly overtaken Estonia despite popular claims.

stories.headline: Lloyds Banking Group acquires Lithuanian fintech Curve Europe with Bank of Lithuania approval
stories.summary: The UK's Lloyds Banking Group received Bank of Lithuania approval to indirectly acquire Curve Europe, a Vilnius-registered electronic money institution. The deal was described as a signal of Lithuania's maturity as a fintech hub and its attractiveness to major international financial institutions.

stories.headline: Ruginienė communication team controversy as new adviser hired and interview format debated
stories.summary: Reports emerged that former Seimas Speaker Graužinienė's adviser Rosvaldas Gorbačiovas is set to join PM Ruginienė's communications team. Separately, a controversial interview with Ruginienė conducted by political commentator Rima Urbonaitė on Laisvės TV triggered a public debate about journalistic standards and the boundaries of political interviewing.
